Please review the following manuscript. I've poured days of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-5st95a5z/call-5d3e0ada8ff943b7a755faa8cda2dc96/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.util
print(sys.version)
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs
python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    texts.append(f'\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:2]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-07.txt tmp/pdfs/page-08.txt tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
scratch = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for page in range(1, 13):
    for suffix in ('txt', 'png'):
        (scratch / f'page-{page:02d}.{suffix}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(scratch / 'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important microscopy problem through interpretable inverse rendering without requiring annotated training datasets. Explicit mesh outputs have clear potential value for geometric measurements and downstream biophysical modeling.

The integration of surface-supported fluorophore densities, differentiable triangle Fourier transforms, CUDA acceleration, and PSF-dependent spectral truncation constitutes a useful technical contribution. Figure 6 demonstrates substantial acceleration of the rendering computation.

Experiments cover several synthetic shapes, 15 mouse organoid volumes, and qualitative examples across three species and microscopy modalities. Figure 9 reports meaningful improvements in image agreement over DM3D: MSE decreases from 0.0125 to 0.0020, while SSIM increases from 0.7101 to 0.8021.

The pipeline is clearly illustrated, relevant methods and data contributors are credited, and a versioned software archive is cited. The discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations of the PSF model and the difficulty of extending to spatially varying optics.
weaknesses: The central claim of accurate cell-shape inference lacks independent quantitative validation. Sections 6.1–6.3 primarily evaluate rendered-image agreement, even when synthetic ground-truth surfaces are available. The DM3D comparison renders both outputs using deltaMic's inferred PSF and evaluates metrics closely related to deltaMic's fitting objective. This demonstrates improved image fitting but does not establish improved geometry. Surface-distance measurements on synthetic data and independently assessed boundaries on real data would substantially strengthen the scientific case.

Joint shape and PSF recovery is insufficiently validated. Section 6.1 uses the same known Gaussian PSF for rendering and inference, while the real-data experiments report neither PSF estimation errors nor comparisons with calibrated or fixed PSFs. Consequently, the evidence does not establish whether recovered optical parameters are accurate or compensate for errors in geometry and fluorophore modeling.

Robustness evidence is narrow: Figure 8 evaluates one synthetic reference shape, limited initialization perturbations, and random noise without specifying its distribution or repeated-trial protocol. Multicell initialization assumes the correct cell count. Sensitivity to the diffusion-smoothed updates with λ = 50 is also unreported; the absence of an explicit regularization penalty does not establish how much reconstruction quality depends on this geometric prior.

Practical scalability and reproducibility need stronger characterization. Figure 6 benchmarks Fourier kernels, including an 80-triangle mesh, whereas applications involve 1,000–10,000 vertices and thousands of optimization steps. End-to-end runtime and peak memory for these applications are missing, as is an accuracy–speed evaluation of the 1% spectral cutoff. Learning rates, image-intensity normalization, and enforcement of valid PSF covariance matrices are insufficiently specified.

Several mathematical expressions require reconciliation. Under the stated Fourier convention, the Gaussian transform in Section 3.2 should be exp(-ξᵀΣξ/2), whereas the manuscript uses Σ⁻¹. The claimed equivalent linear system in Section 5.1 also conflicts with the preceding smoothed update. These appear potentially correctable and do not by themselves invalidate the implementation, but consistent equations and numerical gradient checks are needed. The more consequential concern remains the missing independent evidence for geometry and PSF accuracy.
